currencies.name: US dollar
currencies.summary: Hot core broke the October-hold thesis: October 27–28 a coin flip (~43–54%, from ~23%), December fully priced, DXY a new 18-month high (~102.8) — though the bid partially faded into the close as yields settled (2Y 4.80%). The crowded longs got paid, not squeezed.

policy.note: October 27–28: ~43–54% across afternoon snapshots (from ~23%); December effectively fully priced — own-bank more hawkish vs every peer

growth.note: Home sales beat +1.5% to 3.99m; bank earnings mixed-to-solid — growth leg unchanged

inflation.note: Hot CPI on both core measures (0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y) — own-bank hawkishness validated

risk.note: Post-CPI bid was a rate repricing, not a fear bid

tot.note: No direct terms-of-trade read for the dollar

positioning.note: USD aggregate longs ~$35.5bn rewarded by the hot print — now even more crowded into PPI; unwind risk on any soft number

currencies.name: Euro

policy.note: Fed-ECB gap widened against the euro as October revived; ECB Oct ~12%, December the live meeting

inflation.note: German WPI +8.7% y/y, hottest since Feb 2023 — pipeline inflation firms the December-hike case

risk.note: Crude ~$106 is bearish for the energy-importing eurozone

tot.note: Brent premium (~$106) raises import costs for eurozone buyers

positioning.note: Net shorts -99,332 (~0th pctile) — got paid today; squeeze setup still loaded, trigger denied

fiscal.note: Budget cleared first hurdle (236–149); revenue vote Oct 20, Moody's Oct 23 still ahead

policy.note: Rate gap still favors USD, but the pair faded the whole post-print bid — pace capped into the BoJ's December lean (Oct ~9%, Dec >80%)

growth.note: Japan machinery orders tonight 6:50pm CT — no new data yet

inflation.note: CGPI miss (6.8%) keeps BoJ hike view alive without forcing October

method: per-currency pillar drivers -1/0/+1 from the morning engine reads; positioning scored by the single contrarian rule (stretched longs >=90th pctile = -1, stretched shorts <=10th pctile = +1)
